title: High resolution negative silicone rubber impressions for technological studies
author: Stefano Viola
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bp2ymqfw
materials: Demoulding phase II Gestures: like in phase 5
Rinsing. Use of paintbrush and demineralised water. Water

steps.title: Wash object
steps.instruction: Hold the piece and clean it first with demineralised water, then with acetone, using a soft clean toothbrush or cotton for about 3 min.

steps.title: Dry object in envelope
steps.instruction: Place the piece in an open resealable envelope and let it dry completely for about 30 min at ~18 °C to avoid dust settling.

steps.title: Prepare adhesive support
steps.instruction: Make an adhesive‑paste support that blocks the bead and will contain the silicone; do not apply any release‑agent layer because the object is hard stone.

steps.title: Set up dispenser gun
steps.instruction: Load the Coltene microSystem® Dispenser gun MKII with a jet‑bite cartridge, attach the mixing tip and oral tip, and prime the system.

steps.title: Inject silicone into drill A
steps.instruction: Working time 1 min: inject impression material into drill hole A (three impressions) using the dispenser gun; first eject a small amount of mixed fluid to purge air, then fill the tip completely to avoid an air column (≈30 s).

substeps.instruction: Eject a small amount of mixed fluid and discard it.
Fill the tip fully to prevent air injection.
Inject starting from the bottom of the biconical hole, moving in a circular motion while keeping the tip axial, and continue upward to fill the void.

steps.title: Cover surface A
steps.instruction: Spread silicone over surface A by continuous injection, advancing regularly to prevent air bubbles; leave excess material to ease later demoulding.

steps.title: Allow silicone to set
steps.instruction: Let the silicone harden; demoulding time is approximately 2 min after injection starts.

steps.title: Demould first impressions
steps.instruction: Gently remove the hardened silicone from drill A and surface A by hand or with plastic tweezers, using a continuous delicate motion.

steps.title: Change oral tip
steps.instruction: Replace the mixing tip and its terminal (oral tip) with a fresh one before the second injection series.

steps.title: Inject silicone into drill B
steps.instruction: Working time 1 min: repeat the injection procedure for drill hole B (three impressions) as done for drill A, including the 30 s tip‑priming steps.

substeps.instruction: Eject a small amount of mixed fluid and discard it.
Fill the tip fully to prevent air injection.
Inject from the bottom of the hole with circular, axial motion, filling upward.

steps.title: Cover surface B
steps.instruction: Spread silicone over surface B in the same manner as surface A, maintaining regular advance to avoid bubbles and leaving excess material.

steps.title: Allow second set to set
steps.instruction: Let the silicone harden; demoulding time is again about 2 min.

steps.title: Demould second impressions
steps.instruction: Remove the hardened silicone from drill B and surface B gently with plastic tweezers or by hand.

steps.title: Inspect molds microscopically
steps.instruction: Examine each mold under a microscope for imperfections, air bubbles, or other defects.

steps.title: Store molds
steps.instruction: Place the finished molds in resealable plastic bags and keep them at room temperature.

steps.title: Final wash of object
steps.instruction: Remove any silicone residue by washing the piece with distilled water and acetone using a paintbrush; first apply distilled water with dishwashing surfactant, then rinse with distilled water and acetone to eliminate any silicone‑oil halo.

substeps.instruction: Apply distilled water mixed with dishwashing surfactant using a paintbrush.
Rinse with acetone to remove silicone‑oil traces.

steps.title: Final dry of object
steps.instruction: Air‑dry the object completely for about 15 min at ~18 °C.
